data.name: CustomExeNameInfo
data.value:
Some games implement a block that causes DS4 input to be ignored if a game detects either PhantomPad.exe or InputMapper.exe running at the time. A workaround to the block is to rename PhantomPad.exe so the check in the game fails. Specifying a custom exe name here allows DS4Updater to automatically update a custom copy of PhantomPad to the desired file name. Make sure to omit the extension.
Example: whyme_PhantomPad

data.name: StickFuzzTooltip
data.value: Fuzz specifies the minimum number of units the analog stick moves, in active zone, before the output is registered as changed in the mapper. This setting can be useful for worn sticks that cannot maintain a constant position. The value is expressed in raw stick units.

data.name: StickMaxOutputForceTooltip

data.name: StickMaxOutputTooltip
data.value: In some situations, it might be useful to limit the maximum value that is output by the output analog stick. Max Output allows throttling the final output value of the analog stick.

data.name: AntiDeadzoneTooltip
data.value: An anti-deadzone acts as an offset for use with an axis to denote the minimum output value generated after an axis has left its assigned deadzone. This is mainly meant to help with mapping an axis to the assigned deadzone value used for an axis in a video game. For example, the typical assigned deadzone for XInput LS in a video game is around 8000 (25%). With no anti-deadzone assigned, an axis would have to move past the assigned deadzone in PhantomPad along with the game's assigned axis deadzone.

data.name: SASteeringWheelFuzzTooltip
data.value: Fuzz specifies the minimum number of device units, in active zone, that the Accel has to be rotated before the output is registered as changed in the mapper. The value is expressed in raw Accel units.

data.name: StickRotationTooltip
data.value:
+ = Clockwise. - = Counter-clockwise.
The rotation setting is meant to help correct the orientation of an analog stick if your thumb is slightly shifted when moving an analog stick. For example, your thumb might be slightly shifted from center when the analog stick is moved fully north. My thumbs shift slightly to the right when moving an analog stick fully north due to the way my hands grip the DS4. The value used denotes the number of degrees used to adjust the final axis output value. Values allows range from -180 to 180. Default is 0.

data.name: DualSRumbleForceGenericRescale_Tip
data.value:
Recommended to be left DISABLED.
- Disabled: rumble will be rescaled natively by the controller accordingly to the defined power level (better quality)
- Enabled: both PhantomPad generic rumble rescale and DualSense's native control will be active

data.name: DualSRumbleModes_Tip
data.value:
Accurate Mode (recommended): - Better replicates the DualShock 4/Xbox 360 controller rumble feeling - More accurately executes game's intended rumble effects - Rumble has more depth. Within the same power level there is a greater difference between min and max in-game rumble activation, varying from real low up to the max strength of the defined power level
Legacy Mode: - Overral stronger, but lacks depth - Has a "sharper" feeling - The min and max activation in-game will be, respectively, only slightly below and slight above the chosen power level strength
Disabled: - Fully disables rumble

data.name: DualSRumblePowerLevel_Tip
data.value:
DualSense's native rumble Power Level rescaler.
- When in Accurate Mode, rumble's [ min // max ] will be [ 1% /// Chosen Power Level ] - Example (62%): [ min = 1% /// max = 62% ]
- When in Legacy Mode, rumble's [min /// max ] will be roughly [ Power Level - 12% /// Power Level + 12% ] - Example (62%): [ min = 50% /// max = 74% ]

data.name: PP_StartIntro
data.value: How PhantomPad opens and what closing the window does. Each option has its own switch to turn it on or off.

data.name: PP_StartWithWindowsText
data.value: Opens by itself when the PC turns on.

data.name: PP_StartHiddenText
data.value: When it opens no window appears, only the ghost icon next to the clock. Click the icon to see it.

data.name: PP_StartCloseTray

data.name: PP_StartCloseTrayText
data.value: The X hides the window and PhantomPad keeps working, without asking. To quit completely: right-click the icon → Exit.

data.value: When PhantomPad opens, controllers that are on are ready to play without pressing "Start". If you turn it off, you will have to press "Start" every time.

data.name: PP_StartTip

data.name: PP_UpdIntro
data.value: PhantomPad looks for new versions when it opens and when you come here. If there is one, you can download it while you play: it is not installed by itself, only when you press "Restart app".

data.name: PP_UpdNotConfigured
data.value: Updates are not set up yet

data.name: PP_UpdNotConfiguredText
data.value: You have version {0}. To receive updates, PhantomPad must first be published on GitHub.

data.name: PP_UpdAvailableText
data.value: You have version {0}. Download it while you play; it is only installed when you restart the app.

data.name: PP_UpdManualText
data.value: You have version {0}. This copy was not installed with the PhantomPad installer, so download the new version from its page.

data.name: PP_UpdDownloadingText
data.value: You can keep playing. Nothing is installed until you press "Restart app".

data.name: PP_UpdReadyText
data.value: Press "Restart app" when you finish playing: PhantomPad closes, installs version {0} and opens again.

data.name: PP_UpdErrorText
data.value: Check your internet connection and try again. ({0})

data.name: PP_UpdNote
data.value: Updates come from PhantomPad's official GitHub page. Since PhantomPad is not digitally signed yet, Windows may show a SmartScreen warning when installing it: choose "More info" → "Run anyway".

data.name: PPC_UpdateReady
data.value: The update is downloaded. Press "Restart app" when you want to install it.

data.name: PP_DefsIntro
data.value: PhantomPad recognizes these controllers. If you have one it does not recognize (for example a generic controller), you can add it here without waiting for an update. Everything is saved in the Mandos.json file.

data.name: PP_DefsNoUnknown
data.value: All connected controllers are recognized. If yours does not appear, connect it by USB or Bluetooth and press "Search again".

data.name: PP_DefsOptions
data.value: If something does not work with this controller, turn on what applies:

data.name: PP_DefsOptNoOutput

data.name: PP_DefsOptNoBattery
data.value: It does not report the battery

data.name: PP_DefsOptNoGyroCalib
data.value: No gyro calibration (recommended for generic controllers)

data.name: PP_DefsNoCustom
data.value: You have not added any controller yet.

data.name: PP_DefsNote
data.value: Changes are used when the controller is connected again (or when you press Stop and Start). If you turn off a built-in controller, PhantomPad stops using it.

data.name: PPC_ControllerDefsNotSaved

data.name: PP_HideIntro
data.value: PhantomPad turns each controller into a virtual Xbox controller, so it works in every game and gets all the improvements. To keep games from also seeing the physical controller (and getting every button twice), PhantomPad hides it while it is running. When you stop or close PhantomPad, the controllers are shown again.

data.name: PP_HideDriverOkText
data.value: Official free driver by Nefarius. PhantomPad uses it to hide the physical controllers.

data.name: PP_HideDriverRebootText
data.value: HidHide was installed. It starts working after restarting the PC.

data.name: PP_HideDriverMissingText
data.value: Without it, some games see two controllers (the physical one and the virtual Xbox one) and the buttons get doubled. It is free and official (by Nefarius, the same author as ViGEmBus). You will need to restart the PC afterwards.

data.name: PP_HideToggle
data.value: Hide the physical controllers from games

data.name: PP_HideToggleText
data.value: On: games only see the virtual Xbox controller of each controller (one per controller, also for co-op). Off: games see both.

data.name: PP_HideStateHidden
data.value: Hidden · games only see the virtual Xbox controller

data.name: PP_HideTip
data.value: If a game was already open before you connected the controller, close it and open it again so it stops seeing the physical one.

data.name: PP_HideErrOpen
data.value: Could not talk to HidHide. Restart the PC and try again.

data.name: PP_HideErrInverse
data.value: HidHide is in "inverse" mode. Turn that option off in the HidHide app so PhantomPad can hide the controllers.

data.name: PP_HideLogHidden
data.value: Physical controller hidden from games (they only see the virtual Xbox one)

data.name: PP_XboxToggleText
data.value: Xbox 360, One, Series and compatible controllers also get their own virtual Xbox controller with all the improvements (curves, dead zones, aim sensitivity, turbo...) and are hidden from games like the others. Xbox controllers have no light bar or gyro.

data.name: PP_DrvIntro
data.value: PhantomPad needs two official, free drivers by Nefarius. They come inside PhantomPad, nothing is downloaded.

data.name: PP_DrvViGEmText
data.value: Creates the virtual Xbox controller that games see. Required.

data.name: PP_DrvHidHideText
data.value: Hides the physical controller from games so buttons are not doubled. Recommended.

data.name: PP_DrvRebootNote
data.value: Done. Restart the PC so HidHide starts working. Save what you have open before restarting.

data.name: PP_DrvAllOk
data.value: Everything is installed. PhantomPad is ready.

data.name: PP_DrvNote
data.value: When you press "Install all", the official installers open one after the other: accept the Windows notice and follow their steps. HidHide asks to restart the PC at the end. You can also install them later from Settings → Hide controllers.

data.name: PP_UninCardText
data.value: Removes PhantomPad, its settings, ViGEmBus and HidHide, as if they had never been installed. Useful to try the installer from scratch.

data.name: PP_UninIntro
data.value: This leaves the PC as if PhantomPad had never been installed. These steps are done in order:

data.name: PP_UninSettingsText
data.value: Profiles, calibrations, games, commands and all PhantomPad options. If you turn this off they are kept for a future installation.

data.name: PP_UninNote
data.value: Windows will ask for permission for each driver. PhantomPad closes at the end. Then restart the PC before trying the installer.

data.name: PP_UninStepStop
data.value: Stop PhantomPad and show the hidden controllers again

data.name: PP_UninAppNotInstalled
data.value: this copy was not installed with Setup.exe: only the settings are deleted

data.name: PP_UninFinished
data.value: PhantomPad, ViGEmBus and HidHide were uninstalled. Restart the PC before trying the installer again.

data.name: PP_UninFinishedAsk
data.value: PhantomPad, ViGEmBus and HidHide were uninstalled. You must restart the PC before trying the installer again. Restart now?

data.name: PP_SrcIntro
data.value: Like Playnite, each game takes its data first from its own store and then from general databases. The first source that has each piece of data wins, and nothing you edited is ever changed.

data.name: PP_SrcStoreText
data.value: Epic: the catalog the Epic launcher keeps on your PC (cover, background, description). GOG: GOG's public database. No accounts.

data.name: PP_SrcSteamText
data.value: Description in your language, genres, year, developer and images, if the game is also on Steam. No account; only the game name is sent.

data.name: PP_SrcIgdbText
data.value: The database Playnite uses: almost every game, also the ones you add by hand (descriptions in English). It needs two free keys from a Twitch developer account.

data.name: PP_SrcAuto
data.value: Download data automatically for new games

data.name: PP_SrcSecretSaved
data.value: (saved; leave it empty to keep it)

data.name: PP_SrcHowTo
data.value: How to get the keys (free, once): 1) Go to dev.twitch.tv/console and sign in with a Twitch account (it asks to turn on two-step verification). 2) "Register your application": name PhantomPad, OAuth redirect URL http://localhost, category "Application Integration", client type "Confidential". 3) Copy the Client ID, press "New Secret" and copy the Client Secret here. The secret is saved encrypted for your Windows user.

data.name: PP_SrcNeedKeys
data.value: To use IGDB, write the Client ID and the Client Secret.

data.name: PP_SrcBadKeys
data.value: the Client ID or the Client Secret is not correct
